original.target_description: EFCAB4B SNP rs11062745: allele-frequency ratio for ME/CFS cases versus Kaviar reference controls in Perez et al. Table 1. The located outcome is SNP frequency, not a direct functional assay of the gene.

n.sample_role: ME/CFS participants and Kaviar reference controls; SNP-specific analytic denominators not established
n.exclusions: HIV infection or dementia precluding full participation/consent excluded at eligibility; per-SNP exclusions and missingness not reported.
n.location: p. 1, Abstract, Methods (overall cohort only); p. 5, Table 1 (no analytic denominators)
n.quote: 383 ME/CFS participants underwent DNA testing using the commercial company 23andMe.

replication.target_description: EFCAB4B SNP rs11062745: allele-frequency ratio for ME/CFS cases versus openSNP 23andMe controls, reusing original case frequencies. This is a reanalysis, not a new case sample.

n.sample_role: 23andMe control participants with data for this SNP; ME/CFS analytic denominator not reported
n.exclusions: Per-SNP missingness; exact exclusions not documented. Ratios with fewer than 20 control subjects were considered invalid.
n.location: p. 3, Table 1, EFCAB4B (rs11062745) row, N / 23andMe control column

es.location: p. 3, Table 1, EFCAB4B (rs11062745) row, Ratio of CFS to CONTROL / With 23andMe column

p.location: p. 3, Table 1, EFCAB4B (rs11062745) row; no p-value printed for this allele-frequency ratio

reported_success.location: p. 4, Discussion, paragraph beginning "The three genes"
reported_success.quote: The three genes with polymorphisms that remained with the original study criteria of occurring at least twice as often in CFS patients were EFCAB4B, MORN2, and LINC01171

notes: Titles and DOIs verified from the primary PDF title pages. Original table is p. 5; replication Table 1 is p. 3 (the supplied replication p. 5 locator does not exist in the four-page article). Both print frequency ratios, not odds ratios; printed metrics retained without conversion. No SNP-specific p-values are printed. Original total cohort of 383 is not used as analytic n because SNP-specific denominators cannot be established. Replication n is the printed per-SNP control participant count only, not a combined case-control n. Replication author-derived table ratios use the original reported case frequencies with new controls; ALFA is a separate comparison. Success follows the authors' gene-specific narrative verdict, not a significance inference. ALFA ratio is 1.80, below two, although the authors' narrative includes EFCAB4B among the three remaining genes.
